newsitem.title: USA: West U.S. spot power higher on weather, outages.
newsitem.headline: West U.S. spot power higher on weather, outages.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. moved slightly higher Thursday amid forecasts calling for cooler weather in the Northwest as well as planned and unplanned power plant outages, market sources said.
Higher natural gas prices were also cited as helping to support the power market.
"The revised weather forecast is for cooler-than-normal temperatures in the Northwest," said one trader.
Next-day California-Oregon border electricity was last quoted near $16.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with 15.75 on Wednesday.
Palo Verde traded around $17.00-18.00 per MWh, up from around $16.00 on Wednesday.
October Palo Verde was quoted $15.85-15.95, up from $15.75-15.95 on Wednesday, while COB for October was quoted $15.40-15.60, up from $15.25-15.50 on Wednesday.
In addition to cooler weather in the Northwest, traders said the outage early Thursday of a 670-MW unit at the Centralia coal-fired plant in Washington state tightened the regional spot market.
PacifiCorp said the unit, shut due to a boiler tube leak, should be back up by Friday night.

Trade sources also said uncertainties about whether or not the 1,070-MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear generating station in southern California would be taken off-line for short-term maintenance have not been cleared up.

Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, operator of the San Onofre plant, said it is continuing to monitor the performance of pump seals which need maintenance, but hopes to defer the work until the end of November when the unit will shut for scheduled refueling.
"If that (San Onofre 2) and Palo Verde are down at the same time, the market would really tighten up," said another trader.
The 1,221-MW unit 1 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant in Arizona is now coasting down for a 45-day refueling outage which will start Saturday.
